why: The two sides read 'f ≠ 0' differently. A (theorem_5_5_7, universe 0) uses the strong reading: AdmitsBumpFunctions and LocalModel.HasBumpProperty, both with f(x) ≠ 0. B uses the literal reading of Definitions 5.29/5.33: AdmitsBumpFunctionsWeak and HasBumpPropertyWeak, both with f not identically zero. The atlas formulations agree (exists_atlas_iff: a covering set of PX.IsChart charts is the same as an MAtlas equivalent to PX.atlas). B is itself a true theorem: B_holds re-proves it by the project's argument with f(x) ≠ 0 replaced by f ≢ 0. So A_to_B is proved, but only VACUOUSLY: it does not use A, and A's content (the strong notions) says nothing about the weak ones. B ⇒ A fails for a real reason, not for lack of effort. Getting A from B needs weak bumps ⇒ strong bumps, on X or on local models. That is not glue: on a retract there is no translation that moves a bump that is merely nonzero somewhere onto a given point. Each statement is a true equivalence about its own pair of notions.
intended: With the strong reading on both sides (the blind file's BStrong), A ⇔ BStrong is proved: A_to_BStrong and BStrong_to_A, both #rt_check OK, by exists_atlas_iff alone.
overlap: BStrong_to_A: 185 shared project theorems, all from chart compatibility (MPolyfold.IsChart.compatible and Chapter 1-2 sc-calculus lemmas). A_to_B (via B_holds): 220 shared project theorems. These are the same chart machinery plus the lemmas the project's proof of Theorem 5.34 uses: closure_inter_ball_subset, isScSmoothMap_real_of_local, MPolyfold.IsScSmoothMap.real_chart, IsScSmooth.of_contDiffOn_finiteDimensional (with proposition_1_2_4, theorem_1_3_1'). This is expected, because B_holds is the project's argument adapted to the weak reading.
